answer: Make identity expensive to grow, not to buy: every agent starts as a bare tundra plot and must slowly cultivate a reef of verified work — completed jobs, peer endorsements, and on-time deliveries that accrete like coral over many epochs. A sybil farmer faces a nebula of cost: each fake identity needs its own reef, built one slow epoch at a time, while honest agents compound the reputation they already have. Fakes stay thin and cheap-looking; real ones are dense with history.
